justification: Read-only. No migration, no production write, no change to served output. It adds a standing gate and corrects a published number in the retrospective. Standard rather than critical because nothing it does can alter what a customer is shown; the risk is a gate that passes vacuously, which is what the tests target.

falsifiable_check.command: python scripts/validate_controls_provenance.py  # plus: python -m pytest tests/test_controls_provenance.py -q
falsifiable_check.fails_when: Exit 1 if any dcp_setback_controls row is `unverifiable` — no committed script regenerates it AND it lacks source_text + section_ref. Exit 2 if it could not run (no DATABASE_URL, empty table, no writer files found), because nothing verified is not a pass. Predicted BEFORE running: reproducible 534, traceable 535, unverifiable 0. Actual matched exactly. Both failure exits were demonstrated live: exit 2 against an empty writer tree, and exit 1 over a synthetic row carrying no provenance.

pre_impl.existing_data: All 1,069 rows read, not sampled. Column list taken from information_schema (the table uses `lga`, `value_min`/`value_max` — not `council`/`value_m`). Measured: all 382 manual rows carry source_text AND section_ref, 0 orphaned; provision_id populated on 1 row of 1,069 table-wide; pdf_page 185, last_verified_at 972, source_chapter_key 1,069.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Two. (1) The brief expected a traceable/partial/orphaned split among the 382 with orphans to chase; there are none, so that job does not exist. (2) The premise that extraction_method identifies hand-made rows is false — 330 pipeline-labelled rows have no committed literal and 177 manual-labelled rows do, so the honest split is 534/535, worse than the 36% the retrospective published. Separately, services/extracted_data_integrity.value_absent_from_source flags 49 manual rows, but reading them shows unit and ratio derivations ('900mm' -> 0.9, '1 space per 3 dwellings' -> 0.333), not fabrications, so they are NOT reported as untraceable.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Extends rather than duplicates. services/extracted_data_integrity.py checks whether a VALUE is right; scripts/validate_dcp_setbacks.py checks setback SEMANTICS; this checks whether a ROW can be accounted for at all — a row can pass every semantic check and still be unattributable. value_absent_from_source is imported and reused rather than reimplemented. Follows the ground-truth-set shape of scripts/validate_zone_code_validity.py. No new column and no migration: all three states are derived from existing columns, so they cannot go stale. needs_review was considered and rejected because four production routes already consume it.

functions.name: harvest_committed_literals
functions.input: a repository root; globs scripts/*.py and enrichment paths for files mentioning the table
functions.output: a map of every string literal of 25+ chars to the files holding it, parsed via ast
functions.if_none: an empty map makes main() exit 2 rather than reporting every row unattributable, which would be a vacuous failure rather than a finding

functions.name: classify_rows
functions.input: the table rows plus the harvested literal map
functions.output: exactly one of reproducible / traceable / unverifiable per row, with the evidence for it
functions.if_none: a row with no source_text and no section_ref is unverifiable, the only state that fails; whitespace-only values count as absent

functions.name: label_reality_mismatches
functions.input: the fully classified rows, each already carrying its derived provenance state alongside the extraction_method the writer claimed
functions.output: counts of rows whose extraction_method disagrees with the derived state, in both directions
functions.if_none: advisory only — it never affects the exit code, because a real PDF pipeline legitimately holds no hardcoded literal

values.value: the provenance state of each of 1,069 controls
values.read_at: derived at check time from source_text, section_ref and the repo; never stored
values.if_missing: a row missing both provenance fields is reported by id, lga and control_type and the gate exits 1

queries.purpose: read every control row so a provenance state can be derived for each
queries.where_clause: No WHERE clause, deliberately, and it is a read-only SELECT on a 1,069-row table. Filtering to is_current would leave superseded rows unattributed, so they would come back unaccounted for if ever reinstated. The session is read-only with a 30s timeout.

break_it.scenario: The gate passes because it silently classifies everything as traceable, so it can never go red.
break_it.what_happens: Four tests drive the unverifiable state directly — missing source_text, missing ref, ref-only, and whitespace-only. The CLI was also run over a synthetic bad row and returned exit 1.
break_it.how: classify_rows is pure and DB-free precisely so the failing state can be reached in a test. A `return []` mutation fails test_every_row_gets_exactly_one_state.

break_it.scenario: Attribution is invented from prose: a row's text appears in a COMMENT or docstring and the row is called reproducible.
break_it.what_happens: It would, if the harvest grepped source. It parses with ast and only counts real string constants.
break_it.how: test_a_literal_in_a_comment_is_not_harvested asserts the comment case is not attributed.

break_it.scenario: No writer files are found (wrong root, moved directory) and all 1,069 rows are reported unattributable — a 1,069-row false alarm.
break_it.what_happens: Exit 2 with an explicit 'nothing was verified' message, not exit 1.
break_it.how: Demonstrated live against an empty directory. Three states in the exit codes too: 0 pass, 1 finding, 2 could-not-run.

break_it.scenario: A short literal like 'Table 4' matches many rows and manufactures reproducible status.
break_it.what_happens: Literals under 25 characters are not harvested. The shortest real source_text is 30 chars, so the floor costs no recall.
break_it.how: test_a_short_literal_is_below_the_attribution_floor asserts the short case is absent from the harvest.

break_it.scenario: One unparseable writer file aborts the harvest, silently demoting every row to traceable.
break_it.what_happens: SyntaxError is caught per file and the harvest continues.
break_it.how: test_a_syntax_error_does_not_abort_the_harvest pairs a broken file with a good one and asserts the good literal still lands.

break_it.scenario: The label/reality mismatch is treated as a failure, so 330 legitimate pipeline rows block every push.
break_it.what_happens: It is advisory and never touches the exit code. A genuine PDF-extraction pipeline holds no hardcoded text, so absence of a literal is not evidence of a defect. Confirming those rows would mean re-reading council PDFs, which the extraction runbook forbids.
break_it.how: label_reality_mismatches is print-only; the exit code depends solely on the unverifiable count.

break_it.scenario: The new PostToolUse hook fires on every new file and becomes the alarm nobody reads.
break_it.what_happens: It fires only when git check-ignore reports the path ignored AND it is untracked, under four directories. Tested in three directions: ignored+untracked warns, tracked stays silent, out-of-scope stays silent.
break_it.how: git ls-files --error-unmatch was deliberately NOT used as the trigger: at PostToolUse a new file is legitimately untracked, so it would fire on every new file and be ignored within a day. It is printed as the commit-time follow-up instead.

post_merge.db_reset: None. Read-only; no migration and no write. The 1,069 rows are unchanged.
post_merge.manual_verify: Run `python scripts/validate_controls_provenance.py` and confirm 534 / 535 / 0 with exit 0. Then confirm the CI schema-contract job shows the new 'Validate controls provenance' step green. The hook only takes effect in sessions started after merge, since .claude/settings.json is read at session start.
